text.p: Mike Blackburn, chief executive of the Halifax Building Society, said on Monday that he cannot rule out further acquisitions after the society floats on the stock exchange in June.

"Given our ambitions for our customers, shareholders and our members, clearly we are going to develop our business platforms," Blackburn told reporters. "A maxim we have to have is 'never say never'".
Earlier on Monday, Halifax members voted overwhelmingly in favour of proposals to convert the mutually-owned financial institution into a public company and float it on the stock exchange in June.
The flotation is expected to value the Halifax at around 12 billion stg ($19.5 billion).

Asked if the Halifax would have been interested in bidding for the mutual insurer Scottish Amicable, currently the subject of a bidding war, Blackburn said, "Our acquisition of Clerical Medical was a case of getting our retaliation in first."
The Halifax bought Clerical Medical, an insurance company which distributes its products through independent financial advisers, last year.
Blackburn said the board of the Halifax was delighted with the result of the meeting.
"The membership have spoken loud and clear," he said.

Referring to this year's general election in Britain, Blackburn said, "Our vote may not be the biggest exercise in democracy this year but it will certainly be the second. The vote was a ringing endorsement of our strategy."

Blackburn said he wants to build its traditional areas of market leadership, mortgages and deposits, as well as those areas where it has a smaller market share in fragmented markets such as life assurance and other longer term savings products.
